title: Empirical error quantiles raised six-month ENSO 90% interval score loss at 2000-2024 origins
abstract: We tested past error quantiles against a seasonal normal rule for six-month Nino 3.4 forecast intervals. We used revised NOAA ERSSTv5 and GODAS inputs and 300 monthly origins in 2000-2024. All rules shared an earlier-only forecast center. Empirical signed error quantiles raised mean 90% interval score from 2.60901 to 2.80352 C. Normal-minus-empirical gain was -0.19451 C, with conditional 95% three-year block limits of -0.39033 to -0.03686 C. Five- and ten-year limits were also negative. Coverage fell from 89.33% to 85.67%. Extra lower-side miss penalties explained the score loss. A symmetric empirical control gave uncertain score differences. This extends a campaign benchmark with overlapping observations. It does not show that normal physical noise is true or that empirical methods generally fail. Short dependent calibration pools, revised data and conditional intervals limit inference. Code, aggregate evidence, source hashes, audit and a figure are included. Source records stay external.

display.caption: 90% interval scores, observed coverage and paired score gains at 300 monthly origins. Lower scores are better. Limits use three-year circular blocks of annual scores and hold forecast fits fixed.

citations.reason: We adapt its mean and input code and reuse the same snapshots and origins. The new test compares empirical interval bounds with seasonal normal bounds.
Prior heavy-tail test motivated a separate empirical quantile test. Its mean model differs.
Upstream code credit retained from the reused seasonal benchmark.
